data.title: Chat watcher: a loop tick should not wait a full deploy-poll interval for a 'busy' deploy decision

data.body:
Discovered during AS-95 rework cycle 1 (review finding F4, carried forward rather than fixed there — reasoning in the AS-95 rework comment).

SYMPTOM. Between two watcher-loop ticks the loop yields to a pending rebuild so tick N+1 runs against tick N's merged code. makeDeployOps.pendingDeploy() is true when the last evaluate() decided reason 'busy' — and the deploy poll ALWAYS decides 'busy' while a tick is running (decideDeploy's first branch). So after every loop tick the last decision on record is 'busy' even when there is nothing whatsoever to deploy, and the loop logs LOOP-WAIT deploy pending and waits for the next deploy poll to clear it: up to ADVANCE_DEPLOY_POLL_S, 60s in production, once per loop tick. Observed by qa-priya in an isolated harness (run6b, deploy poll 4s): ticks 2, 3 and 4 each waited with nothing to deploy.

NOT A BUG IN THE YIELD. 'busy' honestly means "we never got to work out whether a rebuild is owed", and treating it as not-pending would fire the next tick against the pre-merge container — the exact thing the yield exists to prevent. Bounded, never a hang, and the yield itself is correct (a real rebuild does land strictly between two ticks).

LIKELY FIX. Let the loop trigger one deploy evaluation at settle — deployOps.evaluate({busy:false}) — instead of waiting for the interval, so the wait becomes one poll rather than one minute. That needs care, which is why it is its own task and not an AS-95 add-on: evaluate() is async with no re-entrancy guard (deploying is set two awaits deep inside performDeploy), it shells out to git twice, probes the container over HTTP, and can call restartWatcher (process.exit(70)). A guard plus falsifiers for the concurrent-evaluate case is most of the work.

FILES. apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs — makeDeployOps (pendingDeploy, evaluate), and the poll() branch that consumes it via nextPollAction.

Planned (Owen, on Opus under the Fable fallback). Ground truth: deployPoll() always decides 'busy' while a tick runs (evaluateInner 1190-1242, decideDeploy first rule 553), pendingDeploy() (1281) reads that record, poll() turns it into wait-deploy (2604-2623), and nothing re-evaluates before the next setInterval tick (2812, deployPollS 60) — settle() (2525-2540) never touches deploy ops, so every loop tick waits up to 60 s for nothing. Decision: (1) makeDeployOps.evaluate() coalesces concurrent calls via an inflight promise (finally-cleared) so a second caller is safe; (2) makeWatcher's settle() calls void deployPoll() after loopOps.settle and before resolveSettled — child is null and our lock released, so the decision becomes real within one evaluation instead of one interval. Not touching nextPollAction, pendingDeploy semantics, decideDeploy, or the interval. 8 tests T1-T8 (4 in watcher.test.js, 4 in watcher-main.test.js; T6 is the headline falsifier: busy record + nothing owed => LOOP-FIRE on the next 5 s poll with deployPollS 3600), 8 anchored mutants with exact red sets (settle exists twice in the file — anchor on the resolveSettled neighbour), 11 ACs, predicted host 550/549/1 -> 558/557/1, compose 550/543/7 -> 558/551/7. No seam with AS-98 or AS-115 (neither touches the watcher). Branch feat/AS-102-settle-deploy-evaluate from 5fbacdf, worktree .worktrees/AS-102. Lena implements (warm on makeDeployOps from AS-88; Marcus fallback), Ruben reviews (Priya reviewed all AS-95 loop cycles and observed this symptom; concurrency guard is Ruben's lane). Open Q1 (settle-evaluation vs AS-84 shutdown race) defaults to as-designed with a T9/M9 if the implementer finds a window.

Implementation complete on feat/AS-102-settle-deploy-evaluate, head 5518207 (4 commits from 5fbacdf: 40cbc52 source, d086f54 T1-T4, ec406a3 T5-T8, 5518207 README). Files: apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs, test/watcher.test.js, test/watcher-main.test.js, watch/README.md. Nothing else touched.

FINDINGS FIRST (deviations from plan §1):
F1 — the plan's "existing deploying check stays as a belt" is wrong: it is LOAD-BEARING. Full coalescing makes a poll that arrives during a build JOIN the build's evaluation promise, so it never reaches evaluateInner's if(deploying) heartbeat branch — the AS-87 test hung (20 s timeout) on the first cut. Fix: evaluate() checks `if (deploying) return evaluateGuarded(opts)` BEFORE the coalescing guard. Safe because decide -> performDeploy -> deploying=true is one synchronous run once an evaluation resumes past its probe, so no call can pass the pre-check and then race for the lock. Added mutant M9 (delete the pre-check) -> AS-87 heartbeat red (hang), proving the ordering matters.
F2 — guard variable is `evaluating`, not the plan's `inflight`: `inflight` already exists in makeDeployOps (AS-87's state-fields record, ~line 958).
F3 — plan §1 says pendingDeploy() "reads stale-build -> false as the build completes". It does not: lastDecision is assigned AFTER performDeploy returns, so a settle-started deploy leaves the record at 'stale-build' until the NEXT evaluation confirms current (same as the interval path today; semantics unchanged per plan scope). T8 drives deployPoll() once after the build for that. Also, while a build runs poll() returns at the AS-75 isDeploying() gate with no LOOP-WAIT line — so T8's during-build assertion is "no fire", and its LOOP-WAIT assertion is on the post-build stale-build record (title unchanged).
F4 — the existing AS-95 test (watcher.test.js:1026) never asserts pendingDeploy() on a stale-build record, so M7 predicted {T8, AS-95} came back {T8} only. Recorded, not edited.

Q1 (§9): NO window, no gate added. probeRunning() awaits fetchJsonOrNull — real I/O — while the shutdown chain resolveSettled() -> Promise.all -> race -> finish() -> exit(0) is pure microtasks (3 hops; T5 pins the count). A settle-started evaluation cannot resume past its first await before the process exits. If shutdown arrives AFTER settle (evaluation mid-probe, child null), finish() runs immediately — identical to an interval-started evaluation today. Caveat for the record: this holds because fetchJson does I/O; an injected synchronous probe would open it (harness-only). Q2/Q3 defaults kept.

COUNTS. Host `node --test` in the worktree: 558 tests / 557 pass / 1 skipped / 0 fail (base 550/549/1; +8 as predicted). Compose: /usr/local/bin/docker compose -f apps/chat/compose.yaml -p asc-impl-as102 run --build --rm test -> "Image asc-impl-as102-test Built", 558 / 551 pass / 7 skipped / 0 fail (base 550/543/7; +8), exit 0, torn down with down -v --rmi local. git merge-tree master..branch: clean tree, no conflicts.

MUTANTS (scratch copy of apps/chat under mkdtemp, never the worktree; each applied by a single-match pattern — the watcher settle anchored on its resolveSettled() tail block, since `settle` exists twice; applied-at-site asserted; the 3 watcher test files, 144 cases, run per mutant): 9 applied, 9 red, 0 survivors.
M1 delete `if (evaluating !== null) return evaluating` -> {T1, T3} EXACT.
M2 delete the finally -> {T2, T4, T6, T8} + AS-95 pendingDeploy + AS-75 stale-container / id-mismatch / source-change + AS-84 hydrate / abort + AS-87 heartbeat = 11 red. WIDER than predicted: every existing test that evaluates twice pins the release. In the guard's favour.
M3 delete `void deployPoll()` -> {T5, T6, T7, T8}. WIDER (+T7: no ERROR line; +T8: the build never starts, test times out). Guard's favour.
M4 move deployPoll() before releaseLock() -> {T5} only. NARROWER: T6 stayed green. Re-read per the 2026-09-10 rule: the mutation applied at the intended site (T5's lockPresent-at-call assertion went red). T6 survives because lockIsBusy() is read after `await probeRunning()`, by which point settle() has already run releaseLock() synchronously — the plan's "lockIsBusy sees our own lock" assumed a synchronous read. The same holds in production (the probe is I/O), so there is no reachable defect; T5 is the guard for that ordering.
M5 evaluate({busy:true}) instead of deployPoll() -> {T5, T6, T7, T8}. WIDER (T7/T8 as M3). Guard's favour.
M6 bare deployOps.evaluate() bypassing the F6 catch -> {T7} EXACT (unhandledRejection captured).
M7 drop stale-build from pendingDeploy -> {T8}. NARROWER (see F4).
M8 move deployPoll() after resolveSettled() -> {T5} EXACT (microtask-hop pin: exit unrun on the evaluation's 3rd turn, run on its 4th).
M9 (extra, not in the plan) delete the `if (deploying)` pre-check -> AS-87 heartbeat red (timeout).
Mutant log: scratchpad/agent-developer-lena/AS-102/mutants.json; runner mutants.mjs (host runs, not per-mutant compose builds).

Harness note for the reviewer: watcher-main.test.js `over.deployOps` may now be a function of {paths, log, now, dir}, so T6/T8 run REAL makeDeployOps over the harness's own lock/state paths with a seeded .lattice/tasks board (one in_progress task). T5's "before resolveSettled" is a microtask-order fact and is self-pinning (exitAt[4] === 1), so a Promise-internals change fails loudly instead of going vacuous. AC-11 README sentence added to watch/README.md § Between ticks. Moving to review (--no-auto-review).

Review stage opened (tick watcher:86819 loop tick 14). Ruben reviews at head 5518207 on feat/AS-102-settle-deploy-evaluate, worktree .worktrees/AS-102; deferred last tick because his lane was on AS-115.

PASS (merge) — reviewed cold at 5518207 by Ruben on Opus under the Fable fallback directive; plan and diff read before the implementer's comment, which I read last. Independent mutant battery is PARTIAL under the tick's 17-minute budget (declared below); everything I observed matches or exceeds the plan.

FINDINGS (2, both non-blocking, 0 blocking; both outside the criteria list):
F1 [convention/record] Plan §3 M4 prediction is wrong: moving void deployPoll() before releaseLock() goes red on {T5} only, not {T5,T6}. Cause, verified in evaluateInner: busy is computed as busy || lockIsBusy(nowMs) AFTER the await probeRunning(), and settle() releases the lock synchronously in the same call, so the interval-side lock check never sees our lock; only T5's ordering assertion pins it. Guard holds (observed red), table needs a correcting note like the AS-98 M11 one. Lena reported the same; I confirmed independently.
F2 [convention/test-hygiene] Under M2 (finally cleared) and M3 (settle call deleted) the two-file run does not finish: M3 goes red on {T5,T6,T7} (wider than {T5,T6}, guard's favour) and then hangs — T8 (and under M2 T6/T8) wait forever on an evaluation that never comes instead of failing. Red-by-hang is still red, but it cost 240 s per mutant here; a per-test timeout on T6/T8 would make the falsifier fail fast. Not a defect; routed to the task owner as a follow-up note.

MUTANTS (scratch copies under /tmp via scratchpad/agent-qa-ruben/as102-mutants.mjs; each anchored on a unique string, anchor count asserted == 1, diff printed before the run): M1 red {T1,T3} EXACT. M2 red-by-hang (see F2). M3 red {T5,T6,T7}+hang (wider). M4 red {T5} (narrower, F1). NOT independently driven within budget: M5, M6, M7, M8, and my three probes (P1 delete the if(deploying) fast path — expected AS-87 heartbeat red; P2 coalesced call returns a fresh noop instead of the first promise — expected T1; P3 deployPoll busy:true at the interval site — expected T5/T6). Implementer reports M5-M8 red; I did not reproduce them. The runner is ready; ~1 min per mutant if the orchestrator wants the battery completed before merge.

COUNTED RUNS: host (worktree, node --test): 558 tests / 557 pass / 1 skipped / 0 fail, exit 0 — exactly plan §5 (+8 over master's 550/549/1). Compose -p asc-review-as102 run --build --rm test: receipt 'Image asc-review-as102-test Built', 558 / 551 pass / 7 skipped / 0 fail, exit 0 — exactly AC-10. Project torn down after this comment.

DESIGN READ: the deploying-first ordering in evaluate() is correct and load-bearing (a poll that joined the build's evaluation would skip evaluateInner's AS-87 heartbeat branch) — I agree with the departure from the plan's 'belt' wording. §9 Q1: no window — finish() reaches exit(0) over microtasks only while the settle-started evaluation is parked on a real fetch in probeRunning(); no shuttingDown gate needed. Coalescing releases correctly on resolve and throw via .finally.

SEAMS: git merge-tree --write-tree vs master ab3aa8e clean; vs feat/AS-115-copy-refs bbec302 clean; branch touches only apps/chat/{watch/advance-watcher.mjs,watch/README.md,test/watcher.test.js,test/watcher-main.test.js}; no .lattice files; 4 commits all developer-lena identity.

FLOOR CHECK (sweep, labelled as such): AC-1 partial (M4/M5/M6 process followed; probes P1-P3 not run), AC-2 pass (T6 red under M3 observed), AC-3 pass (T5 red under M3/M4 observed), AC-4 pass (M1), AC-5 pass by hang (M2), AC-6 pass (T3 under M1), AC-7 not independently falsified (M7), AC-8 partially (T7 red under M3, M6 not driven), AC-9 pass on counts, mutant sets differ per F1/F2, AC-10 pass with receipt, AC-11 pass (README sentence present). 9 of 11 fully observed, 2 partial, 2 findings outside the list. Nothing fixed inline.

Addendum (Ruben): the mutant battery finished after the verdict was recorded — M5 red-by-hang (same shape as F2), M6 red {T7} EXACT, M7 red {T8} only (narrower than plan §3's '{T8} plus the AS-95 test at watcher.test.js:1026' — that test never asserts pendingDeploy() on a stale-build record; guard holds, add to the F1 correcting note), M8 red {T5} EXACT. Independent tally: 8 of 8 plan mutants red (6 by assertion on the recorded sets, M2 and M5 by hang), 0 survivors. Probes P1-P3 were still running at the tick ceiling and are the only thing not independently observed. Verdict unchanged: PASS (merge). Compose project asc-review-as102 torn down (down -v --rmi local, exit 0; compose ls -a shows no leftover).

Merged to master daa74b7 (--no-ff) after Ruben's PASS at 5518207; records export committed bbf5dcb (no ~~human~ file, two public files appended; deploy-state runningId == desiredId at 22:30Z); master pushed; worktree and local branch removed (never pushed, no remote branch). Plan §10 carries Ruben's F1 correcting note. Left open: Ruben's three own probes past the list were cut by the tick ceiling — runner in his scratchpad; non-blocking.
